### Factual Comparison of All-NBA Selections

| Category | Michael Jordan | LeBron James |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **All-NBA First Team** | 10 [jordan_accolades_160, T1] | 13 [lebron_accolades_160, T2] |
| **All-NBA Second Team** | 1 [jordan_accolades_160, jordan_accolades_240, T1] | 4 [lebron_accolades_160, lebron_accolades_240, T2] |
| **All-NBA Third Team** | 0 [T1] | 4 [lebron_accolades_240, T2] |
| **Total All-NBA Selections** | 11 [T1] | 21 [T2] |

---

### Analysis of Tradeoffs

* **Total Volume and Longevity:**  
  LeBron James holds a clear advantage in cumulative volume across every tier, totaling 21 All-NBA honors compared to Michael Jordan's 11 [T1, T2]. James leads in First Team selections (13 to 10), Second Team selections (4 to 1), and Third Team selections (4 to 0) [T1, T2].

* **Selection Distribution:**  
  Jordan’s All-NBA selections are overwhelmingly concentrated at the First Team level: 10 of his 11 total selections (approximately 90.9%) were First Team honors [T1]. By comparison, James earned 13 First Team selections while also maintaining an All-NBA standard across an extended career, adding 8 combined Second and Third Team selections [T2].

---

### Separation of Evidence from Subjective GOAT Judgments

* **Factual Evidence:** Objectively, LeBron James holds more All-NBA selections in every individual category (First, Second, and Third Team) as well as total selections [T1, T2].
* **Subjective GOAT Considerations:** In discussions of basketball greatness, evaluators weigh these numbers differently. Proponents of LeBron James view the 21 total selections and 13 First Team nods as evidence of unprecedented sustained elite play and longevity [T2]. Conversely, proponents of Michael Jordan emphasize his rapid accumulation of 10 First Team nods across a shorter active career, interpreting the near-total concentration of First Team awards as an indicator of absolute peak dominance [T1]. Deciding which profile is superior depends on individual valuation of peak dominance versus career longevity.
